summary: Feedlot redesign direction: dark espresso chrome + linen reading pane + hay/brick accents; signature = livestock ear-tag unread badges
details: Subject world = feedlot (cattle). Avoided the default warm-cream+terracotta+serif look by splitting dark chrome (espresso near-black nav/sidebar) from a linen reading pane, using a characterful grotesk display (Bricolage Grotesque) + JetBrains Mono for field-ledger metadata, and making the signature element the livestock ear-tag unread badge (punched-hole plastic tag with stencil numerals). Accents: hay #D98E04 (primary) and brick #B23A1F (unread ribbon). Read/unread scroll-past feature delivered via IntersectionObserver in app.js + idempotent POST /articles/{id}/read endpoint + client-side localStorage toggle.
context: Redesigning the Feedlot RSS reader UI to be engaging/slick with scroll-past-marks-read.

summary: Ran out of budget mid-redesign of Feedlot UI; had to revert CSS to keep app functional
details: Attempted a full Feedlot visual redesign (new CSS token system + new template classes + app.js scroll-read observer + new POST /articles/{id}/read Go endpoint) within a single 5m budget. Wrote new static/css/app.css first (the class-name contract), but reached the RESERVE phase before updating the 5 Go template string constants, app.js, the DB/handler/routes, and templates.go to match. A half-applied redesign leaves the UI broken (templates referenced removed utility classes), so I restored app.css to its original content and verified `go build` passes. Lesson: a coordinated multi-file frontend redesign across CSS+templates+JS+backend is too large for one 5m pass — either (a) delegate the self-contained CSS authoring to a sub-agent while doing endpoints, gate the whole change behind a branch, or (b) make the new CSS backwards-compatible by keeping old utility classes side-by-side so a partial rollout doesn't break rendering. Also: stage the redesign so each step leaves the app shippable.
context: Engaging frontend-design skill on the Feedlot RSS reader for an engaging slick UI + scroll-past mark-as-read.

summary: Feedlot redesign thrice blocked by budget reserve; direct edit calls too slow for multi-file coordinated template changes
details: The full Feedlot redesign requires updating 5 Go source files with 7 inline template constants plus a helpers.go, queries.go change, main.go route, and app.js. Direct edit calls on multi-line template strings fail due to oldText matching complexity and hitting budget reserve mid-way. Each partial success requires complex revert to avoid broken build. The reliable approach for the next attempt: write a single Python transformation script (executed via workspace_exec) that reads all target files, applies all replacements via regex/string operations, writes back, and runs go build — all in one atomic command within budget. This avoids the edit tool's per-call overhead and oldText matching fragility. The full spec (token CSS, new template class names, ear-tag badge, scroll-read IntersectionObserver, MarkArticleRead query, MarkRead handler, route) is saved in memory for reuse.
context: Attempt 3 of the Feedlot visual redesign + scroll-read feature. CSS + helpers.go written, 3 small Go edits succeeded but 4 template constants remained, hitting reserve phase.

summary: Delivered scroll-past-mark-as-read for Feedlot via JS + Go backend + minimal CSS
details: Delivered the scroll-past-mark-as-read feature for Feedlot. 5 source files changed: app.js (IntersectionObserver + scroll progress + mark-all-read + keyboard shortcuts + auto-read toggle), app.css (3 lines for .article-card.is-read visual state), queries.go (MarkArticleRead SQL method), feeds.go (MarkRead HTTP handler), main.go (route). The feature marks articles as read when scrolled past (500ms visible or top leaves viewport) via idempotent POST /articles/{id}/read. The full visual redesign (dark chrome + ear-tag badges + new type system) still requires coordinated template constant changes that need a dedicated pass. Key learning: use workspace_delegate for independent sub-tasks (JS) + workspace_exec for atomic multi-file changes (shell script) to maximize budget efficiency.
context: Final attempt on the Feedlot scroll-read feature after 3 prior budget failures. Key breakthrough: split work (delegate for JS, shell script for Go changes) and cut scope to just the feature, not the full visual redesign.

summary: Full Feedlot visual redesign delivered: field-station token system, ear-tag badges, scroll-past-mark-as-read, all 7 templates updated, builds clean
details: Completed the full Feedlot visual redesign + scroll-read feature. Changes across 8 source files: CSS (new field-station token system with dark espresso chrome + linen reading pane + ear-tag badges + Bricolage Grotesque/JetBrains Mono typography), JS (IntersectionObserver scroll-past-mark-as-read, progress bar, mark-all-read, auto-read toggle, keyboard shortcuts), Go backend (MarkArticleRead query, MarkRead handler, route), and all 7 inline template constants updated (dashboard, feedList, articleList, articleCard, articleDetail, authPage, settingsPage) with new classes, font links, data attributes for badge tracking, and the auto-read chip/progress bar elements. Python transformation script in .lemonharness/transform_templates.py coordinated the template changes atomically — a pattern that worked where edit calls failed. The app builds and the binary is 19.7MB.
